subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 2x² + 3 and g(x) = 3x − 2, find (fog)(x).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.10, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 10(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to substituting g(x) into f in the right order and one to the expansion, because the order of composition and the squaring of a bracket are the two separate skills being tested. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (fog)(x) — which function acts first, and how you expand what is left.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Put g(x) into f
steps.margin_note: First mark. Keep 3x − 2 inside a bracket when it enters f, so the squaring applies to the whole of it.
steps.memory_tip: In fog, g is inside. Read the composition from right to left.
lines: g acts first, so 3x − 2 goes into f:

recall.must_convey: That in fog the inner function is g, so 3x − 2 is substituted into f, giving 2(3x − 2)² + 3.
accept: in f o g the inner function is g so three x minus two goes into f
f of three x minus two is two times three x minus two whole squared plus three
g acts first because it is written second
modata g apply chestham so three x minus two ni f lo pedatham
substitute three x minus two for x in f

steps.why: In fog the function written on the right acts first, so g's output becomes f's input. Writing f(3x − 2) with the bracket kept whole is what makes the next line correct.
common_mistakes: Applying f first, which computes (gof)(x) = 6x² + 7 instead.
Writing f(3x − 2) as 2(3x² − 2) + 3, squaring only the x.

steps.label: Expand and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Square the bracket first, then multiply all three terms by 2, then add the 3. Doing the multiplication before the square is where marks are lost.
steps.memory_tip: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². Here the middle term is −12x, and the 2 outside makes it −24x.

recall.must_convey: That (3x − 2)² expands to 9x² − 12x + 4, and doubling it and adding 3 gives 18x² − 24x + 11.
accept: three x minus two squared is nine x squared minus twelve x plus four
double it to get eighteen x squared minus twenty four x plus eight then add three
the answer is eighteen x squared minus twenty four x plus eleven
expand chesi rendu tho multiply chesi three add chesthe eighteen x squared minus twenty four x plus eleven
the constant is eight plus three which is eleven

steps.why: The bracket is squared before anything multiplies it, and the 2 then multiplies all three terms of the expansion. The constant 11 is 8 from the doubled square plus the 3 that f always adds.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the first term by 2, giving 18x² − 12x + 4.
Writing (3x − 2)² as 9x² + 4 and losing the middle term.
